==============================================================================
7. STRUCTURAL INTERPRETATION
==============================================================================

Experiment 119 showed that the B-odd order-3 / degree-2 operator remains unique after changing from the monomial r-basis to the falling-factorial r-basis.

Experiment 120 therefore treats that operator as the exceptional object and asks whether its uniqueness is accompanied by a simpler coefficient structure or by transfer to another sector.

The important distinction is between:

    exactness:
        the operator reproduces every available transition;

    simplicity:
        its coefficient polynomials have small falling-basis coefficients or factor into lower-order operators;

    universality:
        the same operator mechanism works in more than one sector.

A failure of transfer together with enormous exact coefficients would make the B-odd operator look like a finite-data coincidence.

A successful transfer or factorization would instead provide a genuine construction-level signal.

All arithmetic is exact Fraction arithmetic.
No floating point.
No SymPy.
No extrapolation.
